title: Make SDDC Manager network pool provisioning safe to retry
prompt:
Platform automation ticket for our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 estate. Our network pool provisioning job is run from a scheduler that retries any step it thinks failed, and last week that left us with two SDDC Manager network pools called `np-vi-edge`: the create was accepted, the response was lost behind a gateway error, and the retry created a second pool. Fix the module so a retry can never do that again.

Work in `VcfNetworkPoolProvisioning.psm1` at the workspace root. It already builds the request models and retries a failed create; the retry is what is wrong.

The runner installs the genuine `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` PowerCLI module 13.5.0.25380678 and its `VMware.OpenAPI` dependency as an environment prerequisite. Import and use that SDK: build every request body with its model initializers (`Initialize-VcfIpPool`, `Initialize-VcfNetwork`, `Initialize-VcfNetworkPool`) and make every call with its cmdlets (`Invoke-VcfGetNetworkPool`, `Invoke-VcfCreateNetworkPool`). Do not vendor VMware modules, and do not replace the SDK transport with `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, `HttpClient`, curl, or any other HTTP client.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a projection of `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, at the commit recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. It comes from the specification, not from a documentation page, and not from the 9.1 revision of that same file. The only operationIds in scope are `createToken`, `getNetworkPool` and `createNetworkPool`.

Keep the existing signature:

`Invoke-VcfNetworkPoolProvision -Server <VcfSddcManagerServer> -Name <string> -Network <hashtable[]> [-MaxAttempts <int>] [-RetryDelaySeconds <int>] [-SleepAction <scriptblock>]`

Each `-Network` entry has `Type`, `VlanId`, `Mtu`, `Subnet`, `Mask` and `Gateway`, and optionally `IpPools`, an array of entries with `Start` and `End`.

Required behaviour:

- `createNetworkPool` is not idempotent: SDDC Manager accepts the same specification twice and leaves two pools behind. Every provisioning attempt, including each retry, must therefore read the existing pools with `getNetworkPool` and match on the exact pool name before it considers creating anything.
- If no pool has that name, create it and report `Created`.
- If a pool with that name already exists and matches the requested definition, adopt it and create nothing. Report `AlreadyExists` when the first attempt found it, and `RecoveredAfterRetry` when a later attempt found the pool that an earlier attempt of this same call had created without being able to report it. A pool matches when it carries exactly the requested network types and each of those networks agrees on `vlanId`, `mtu`, `subnet`, `mask` and `gateway`; already-allocated `ipPools` are server state and are not compared.
- If a pool with that name exists with a different network definition, fail with a terminating error naming the pool, and do not write anything.
- Retry the create only when it failed with HTTP 429, 502, 503 or 504, at most `MaxAttempts` attempts in total. Any other failure is terminating. Before each retry, wait `RetryDelaySeconds` by invoking `SleepAction` with that number of seconds when the caller supplied one, and with `Start-Sleep` otherwise.
- Return one object whose properties are, in this order, `Name`, `PoolId`, `Outcome`, `Attempts` and `Pool`, where `Attempts` counts provisioning attempts including the first, and `Pool` is the SDK network pool model. Export only `Invoke-VcfNetworkPoolProvision`.

Send exactly what the 9.0.0.0 contract describes and nothing more. The create body carries only `name` and `networks`; `id` and `hostsCount` are server state. Each network carries only the six members that schema requires, plus `ipPools` when, and only when, the caller supplied ranges for that network: an unset `ipPools` must be omitted from the request rather than sent as `null` or `[]`.

The protected verifier drives the real SDK against a contract-pinned loopback SDDC Manager whose route table is built from `docs/contract.json`, makes one create succeed on the server while losing its response, reads the resulting request log, and checks the exact methods, paths, authentication, JSON member sets and values, the omission of unset optional fields, how many pools were created, and the pools that survive. It does not contact a live VMware endpoint. Run it with `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -File .protected/verify.ps1`.

Only `VcfNetworkPoolProvisioning.psm1` may be changed; `docs/` and `.protected/` are protected fixtures.
